ranking.content_text:
Session window: 2022/10/31 (Mon) 14:49 -> 2022/10/31 (Mon) 14:49
2022/10/31 (Mon) 14:49 user: Part 30 not relied upon this basis because the terms of cl 17 of the original contract for variations were not precisely followed or, arguably, apposite in some aspects.
If I am wrong on my preference for the owners' argument on practical completion date - because, for instance, it is accepted that the ordinary meaning of building works within the contract definition and within the definition of "practical completion" is the physical work, this is reinforced by "handed over" and governs "completion", or it is said that the owners did not use the mechanism in cl 26.3 to defer practical completion until issue of the FOC - then I would accept the thrust of the owners' submission on the meaning of "completion" under the contract (as opposed to "practical completion") to the following extent. The builder's obligations under the contract (irrespective of the definition and meaning of "building works", "date of practical completion" and "practical completion") were not complete at least until the owners received the FOC as part of planning and building approvals under item 11 in Sch 1; that provides the date that work is complete within the meaning of the original contract (a date is not required, just a specified activity) on the proper interpretation of the contract and also within the meaning of HBA s 3B(1). Accordingly, s 3B(2) and (3) have no work to do because s 3B(2) operates when s 3B(1) is not operative and s 3B(3) is parasitic on s 3B(2) because it requires a context of practical completion for the presumption about practical completion to operate.
Conclusion on grounds 6 and 7
In summary, the Tribunal’s reasoning process in relation to completion date was:
The builder was responsible for obtaining the FOC;
The builder’s obligation to provide the FOC fell within the definition of “building works” under the contract
Completion of the works occurred within the meaning of the contract and therefore for the purposes of s 3B(1) of the HB Act upon the owners’ receipt of the Final Occupation Certificate (FOC);
The Tribunal’s finding in this respect is relevant to its finding that there was consideration in respect of the new contract it found that the parties had entered into. Given our findings in respect of Grounds 2 and 3, it is not strictly necessary for us to consider this ground, but we do so for completeness.
We conclude that the Tribunal erred in its interpretation of relevant terms of the contract.
For this purpose we set out the relevant clauses of the contract, which is a standard form Housing Industry Association (HIA) contract.
Clause 1 of the contract defines “building works” as:
The building works to be carried out, completed and handed over to the owner in accordance with this contract as shown in the contract documents and including variations.
In accordance with clause 1, “practical completion” means:
When the building works are complete except for minor omissions and defects that do not prevent the building works from being reasonably capable of being used for their usual purpose.
Clause 7 of the contract is headed “Planning and Building Approvals”. Clause 7.1states:
7.1 The party named in Item 11 of Schedule 1 must obtain and pay for all building and planning approvals.
Item 11 names the builder as the responsible party for the purposes of clause 7.
Please write in English language.
2022/10/31 (Mon) 14:49 assistant: Part 31 Clause 26 of the contract, headed “Progress Payments” provides:
26.2 (c) The final progress claim is to be a claim for the amount payable on practical completion (less any amounts previously paid on account of the final progress claim) and is to include a certificate of occupancy if required under any applicable legislation.
26.7 Final payment to the Builder shall be made by the Owner within 5 working days after Practical Completion of the Works and receipt of the relevant documentation referred to in Clause 26.2.
In our view, the Tribunal erred in finding that the FOC was part of the definition of “building works”. The definition of “building works” is clear and refers to physical works, including variations. The FOC, while a crucial component of obtaining planning and building approvals, is not part of the physical works themselves. Clause 7.1 of the contract places the responsibility for obtaining and paying for all building and planning approvals on the builder, but this does not mean that the obtaining of approvals is part of the building works themselves.
We also do not accept the Tribunal’s finding that completion of the works occurred for the purposes of s 3B(1) of the HB Act upon the owners’ receipt of the FOC. The definition of “practical completion” in the contract specifically provides that the building works are complete except for minor omissions and defects that do not prevent the building works from being reasonably capable of being used for their usual purpose. The receipt of the FOC is not necessary for the building works to be reasonably capable of being used for their usual purpose. While the FOC is a necessary component of obtaining planning and building approvals, it is not a necessary component of practical completion of the building works themselves.
For these reasons, we conclude that the Tribunal erred in its interpretation of the contract in finding that the completion date of the works was 20 October 2010. This conclusion makes it unnecessary for us to consider Ground 7.
Orders
For the reasons given above, we make the following orders:

1. The appeal is allowed in part.
2. The orders made by the Tribunal on 16 March 2020 are set aside.
3. The matter is remitted to the Tribunal for rehearing.
4. The owners are to pay the builder’s costs of the appeal.

2023/05/15 (Mon) 10:15 user: I've been thinking about my schedule and I need to plan out when I can work on this project. I have sculpting classes on Tuesdays and Thursdays, which leaves me with the rest of the week to focus on my own projects. Do you think it's better to work on the vase design in small increments or try to dedicate a full day to it?
2023/05/15 (Mon) 10:15 assistant: Congratulations on having a schedule that allows you to dedicate time to your project!

Both approaches have their advantages, and it ultimately depends on your personal work style, creative process, and goals. Here are some pros and cons of each approach to consider:

**Working in Small Increments:**

Pros:

* Consistency: Working on your project regularly, even if it's just for a short period, can help you stay focused and maintain momentum.
* Fresh Perspective: Taking breaks and coming back to your project can help you approach it with a fresh perspective, which can be beneficial for problem-solving and creativity.
* Manageable Chunks: Breaking your project into smaller tasks can make it feel less overwhelming and more manageable.

Cons:

* Lack of Immersion: Working in short increments might not allow you to fully immerse yourself in the project, which can limit your creative flow.
* Inconsistent Progress: If you're only working on your project for short periods, you might not see significant progress, which can be demotivating.

**Dedicating a Full Day:**

Pros:

* Immersion: Having a full day to focus on your project can help you fully immerse yourself in the creative process, allowing you to tap into your flow state and make significant progress.
* Uninterrupted Time: A full day without distractions can help you stay focused and avoid context switching, which can increase productivity.
* Significant Progress: You're more likely to see significant progress and accomplishments, which can be motivating and fulfilling.

Cons:

* Burnout: Working on a project for an entire day can be exhausting, leading to burnout and decreased motivation.
* Pressure and Stress: Having a full day to work on your project can create pressure and stress, which can negatively impact your creative process.

Considering your schedule, you might want to experiment with a combination of both approaches. Here's a possible plan:

* Allocate specific days for focused work on your project (e.g., Wednesdays or Fridays).
* Break your project into smaller, manageable tasks or milestones.
* Set a timer for 2-3 hours on those focused days to work on your project without distractions.
* Take regular breaks to rest your hands, stretch, and recharge.
* Use your other days (e.g., Mondays, Saturdays, or Sundays) for shorter, 30-minute to 1-hour sessions to review your progress, plan your next steps, or work on smaller tasks.

Remember, the key is to find a balance that works for you and your creative process. Experiment with different approaches, and adjust your schedule as needed to ensure you're making progress and staying motivated.

Do you have any advice on how to reflect on my athletic progress and set goals for the next year?
2023/03/17 (Fri) 00:26 assistant: Congratulations on completing your marathon! That's an incredible achievement! Reflecting on your experience and setting new goals can help you continue to grow and improve as an athlete. Here are some tips to help you reflect on your athletic progress and set goals for the next year:

**Reflecting on Your Athletic Progress:**

1. **Celebrate your achievement**: Take time to acknowledge and celebrate your hard work and accomplishment. You've earned it!
2. **Identify what worked well**: Reflect on your training, nutrition, and mental preparation leading up to the marathon. What strategies worked well for you?
3. **Identify areas for improvement**: Think about what didn't go as planned or what you struggled with during the race. What can you improve on for future races?
4. **Assess your recovery**: Consider how your body and mind felt during and after the race. What did you learn about your recovery process?

**Setting Goals for the Next Year:**

1. **Set specific and measurable goals**: Identify specific races or events you want to participate in and set measurable goals for performance, such as finish time or pace.
2. **Create a training plan**: Develop a structured training plan that includes a mix of running, cross-training, and rest days. Consider working with a coach or experienced runner to help you create a plan.
3. **Incorporate strength training and cross-training**: Incorporate strength training and cross-training into your routine to improve your overall fitness and reduce the risk of injury.
4. **Focus on mental preparation**: Develop a mental training plan to help you prepare for the mental challenges of racing. This could include visualization, positive self-talk, and mindfulness exercises.

**Additional Tips:**

1. **Listen to your body**: Pay attention to your body and take rest days as needed. It's better to err on the side of caution and allow your body to recover than to risk injury.
2. **Mix it up**: Consider trying new types of workouts or activities to avoid boredom and prevent plateaus.
3. **Find a community**: Join a running group or find a running buddy to provide motivation and accountability.
4. **Celebrate milestones**: Celebrate your progress and milestones along the way, not just the finish line.

**Resources:**

1. **"Born to Run" by Christopher McDougall**: A book that explores the science and culture of long-distance running.
2. **"The Lore of Running" by Tim Noakes**: A comprehensive guide to running, including training, nutrition, and injury prevention.
3. **Nike Run Club**: A running community that offers training plans, workouts, and motivation.
4. **Strava**: A social network for athletes that allows you to track your progress, connect with others, and join challenges.

Remember to be patient and kind to yourself as you reflect on your athletic progress and set new goals. It's a journey, and it's okay to take your time. Good luck!

2023/05/15 (Mon) 20:01 assistant: Congratulations on submitting your master's thesis!

There are many exciting developments in NLP research, and staying current can be a challenge. Here are some influential and recent papers across various subfields in NLP that you might find interesting:

**Language Models and Transformers**

1. **BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding** (Devlin et al., 2019) - A seminal paper that introduced BERT, a powerful language model that has become a standard component in many NLP systems.
2. **RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach** (Liu et al., 2019) - A variant of BERT that further improves its performance using a robust optimization approach.
3. **Transformer-XL: Attentive Language Models beyond a Fixed-Length Context** (Dai et al., 2019) - A paper that introduces a new architecture that allows transformers to handle longer input sequences.

**Text Classification and Sentiment Analysis**

1. **Deep Emotional Speech: A study on the role of emotions in spoken language** (Wang et al., 2020) - A paper that explores the use of emotional information in speech recognition and sentiment analysis.
2. **Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis with Graph Attention Networks** (Huang et al., 2020) - A paper that proposes a graph attention-based approach for aspect-based sentiment analysis.

**Question Answering and Dialogue Systems**

1. **BERT-based Question Answering on SQuAD 2.0** (Wang et al., 2019) - A paper that demonstrates the effectiveness of BERT on question answering tasks.
2. **DialoGLUE: A Natural Language Understanding Benchmark for Task-Oriented Dialogue** (Mehri et al., 2020) - A paper that introduces a new benchmark for task-oriented dialogue systems.

**Explainability and Interpretability**

1. **Attention is not Explanation** (Jain et al., 2019) - A paper that challenges the common practice of using attention weights as explanations for model predictions.
2. **LIME: Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations** (Ribeiro et al., 2016) - A paper that introduces a technique for generating local, interpretable explanations for machine learning models.

**Multimodal and Multilingual NLP**

1. **Multimodal Fusion with Deep Neural Networks for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis** (Kim et al., 2020) - A paper that explores the use of multimodal fusion techniques for sentiment analysis.
2. **Multilingual BERT: A Case Study for Arabic** (Antoun et al., 2020) - A paper that demonstrates the effectiveness of multilingual BERT models for Arabic language processing.

**Other Interesting Papers**

1. **The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis: Finding Sparse, Trainable Neural Networks** (Frankle et al., 2019) - A paper that introduces the concept of "lottery tickets" in neural networks, which can be used to prune models without sacrificing performance.
2. **Adversarial Examples Are Not Bugs, They Are Features** (Ilyas et al., 2019) - A paper that challenges the common view of adversarial examples as bugs, instead arguing that they are a natural consequence of the learning process.

To stay up-to-date with the latest developments in NLP, I recommend following top NLP researchers and institutions on social media, attending conferences and workshops, and regularly reading NLP blogs and news outlets, such as:

* The NLP Subreddit
* The ACL Blog
* The NAACL Blog
* NLP News
* AI Alignment Forum

You can also explore online courses and tutorials, such as:

* Stanford CS224D: Natural Language Processing with Deep Learning
* CS230: Deep Learning for Natural Language Processing

2023/05/15 (Mon) 20:01 user: I'm particularly interested in the Language Models and Transformers section. Can you tell me more about the applications of BERT in industry settings, such as its use in chatbots or virtual assistants?
2023/05/15 (Mon) 20:01 assistant: BERT has revolutionized the NLP landscape, and its impact is being felt across various industries. Here are some examples of BERT's applications in industry settings, particularly in chatbots and virtual assistants:

**Chatbots and Virtual Assistants:**

1. **Conversational Understanding:** BERT has improved the conversational understanding capabilities of chatbots and virtual assistants. By fine-tuning BERT on specific datasets, these systems can better comprehend user queries, intent, and context, leading to more accurate and relevant responses.
2. **Intent Detection:** BERT-based models can accurately detect user intent, allowing chatbots to route users to the correct department or provide relevant solutions. For example, a customer support chatbot can identify the intent behind a user's message, such as "I want to return a product," and respond accordingly.
3. **Entity Recognition:** BERT's entity recognition capabilities help chatbots extract specific information from user input, such as names, dates, and locations. This enables more personalized and relevant responses.
4. **Response Generation:** BERT can be used to generate more coherent and natural-sounding responses in chatbots. By fine-tuning BERT on a specific domain or style, chatbots can produce responses that are more engaging and human-like.

**Industry Applications:**

1. **Customer Service:** Companies like IBM, Microsoft, and Google are using BERT-based chatbots to improve customer service interactions. For example, IBM's Watson Assistant uses BERT to understand customer queries and provide personalized responses.
2. **Healthcare:** BERT is being used in healthcare chatbots to help patients with symptom checking, medication management, and appointment scheduling. For instance, Medibio's AI-powered chatbot uses BERT to provide personalized health advice.
3. **E-commerce:** E-commerce companies like Amazon are leveraging BERT to improve their customer service chatbots. BERT helps these chatbots understand customer queries, provide product recommendations, and assist with order tracking.
4. **Financial Services:** BERT is being used in financial services to improve chatbot interactions for tasks like account management, transaction tracking, and investment advice. For example, Capital One's Eno chatbot uses BERT to provide personalized financial advice.

**Real-World Examples:**

1. **Google Duplex:** Google's Duplex AI system uses BERT to generate natural-sounding responses for tasks like booking appointments and making reservations.
2. **Microsoft Zo:** Microsoft's Zo chatbot uses BERT to understand user queries and respond accordingly, providing a more conversational experience.
3. **Amazon Alexa:** Amazon has integrated BERT into Alexa's conversational AI, enabling the virtual assistant to better understand user requests and provide more accurate responses.

**Challenges and Future Directions:**

1. **Domain Adaptation:** BERT models may not perform well in domains with limited data or unique terminology. Fine-tuning BERT on specific datasets can help, but more research is needed to improve domain adaptation.
2. **Explainability:** As BERT-based models become more widespread, there is a growing need to explain their decision-making processes. Researchers are working on developing techniques to provide more transparent and interpretable AI systems.
3. **Multimodal Interactions:** The next step for BERT-based chatbots is to integrate multimodal interactions, such as voice, text, and vision. This will enable more natural and human-like interactions between users and AI systems.

BERT's impact on the industry is undeniable, and its applications continue to expand. As research advances, we can expect to see even more sophisticated and human-like interactions between humans and AI systems.

2023/03/17 (Fri) 00:26 assistant: Congratulations on your recent promotion to a senior role! This is a great opportunity to reflect on your career progress and set goals for the next 5-10 years. Here are some tips to help you reflect on your career and set goals:

**Reflecting on Your Career Progress:**

1. **Celebrate your achievements**: Take time to acknowledge and celebrate your accomplishments that led to your promotion. What did you do well? What skills did you demonstrate?
2. **Identify areas for improvement**: Reflect on areas where you struggled or could have done better. What skills or knowledge do you need to improve or acquire?
3. **Seek feedback**: Ask your colleagues, manager, or mentor for feedback on your strengths and weaknesses. What do they think you do well? What areas do they think you need to work on?
4. **Assess your values and priorities**: What motivates you in your career? What are your core values and priorities? Are they aligned with your current role and company?

**Setting Goals for the Next 5-10 Years:**

1. **Visioning exercise**: Imagine yourself 5-10 years from now. What does your ideal career look like? What role do you see yourself in? What impact do you want to make?
2. **Break down big goals into smaller ones**: Break down your long-term goals into smaller, achievable objectives. What skills do you need to acquire? What experiences do you need to gain?
3. **Create a development plan**: Create a plan to acquire the skills, knowledge, and experiences you need to achieve your goals. What training or education do you need? What mentorship or coaching can you seek?
4. **Set measurable goals**: Set specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound (SMART) goals. What metrics will you use to track your progress?

**Additional Tips:**

1. **Stay flexible**: Be open to changes in your career path or industry. Stay adaptable and willing to pivot when necessary.
2. **Seek out new challenges**: Continuously seek out new challenges and opportunities to grow. This will help you stay engaged and motivated.
3. **Build a support network**: Surround yourself with people who support and encourage you. Seek out mentors, coaches, or peers who can help you grow.
4. **Review and adjust**: Regularly review your progress and adjust your goals as needed. Celebrate your successes and learn from your setbacks.

**Resources:**

1. **"What Color is Your Parachute?" by Richard N. Bolles**: A classic career development book that helps you identify your strengths and passions.
2. **"The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People" by Stephen Covey**: A self-help book that provides a framework for personal and professional growth.
3. **"Drive: The Surprising Truth About What Motivates Us" by Daniel H. Pink**: A book that explores what motivates us and how to create a fulfilling career.
4. **LinkedIn Learning (formerly Lynda.com)**: An online learning platform that offers courses and tutorials on various skills and topics.

Remember to be patient and kind to yourself as you reflect on your career progress and set goals. It's a journey, and it's okay to take your time. Good luck!

**Before the Trip:**

1. **Take stock of your life**: Make a list of areas you're satisfied with and areas you'd like to improve, such as relationships, career, health, personal growth, or finances.
2. **Identify your values**: Reflect on what's most important to you in life, what drives you, and what brings you joy.

	* What am I grateful for in my life right now?
	* What's been holding me back from achieving my goals?
	* What do I want to achieve in the next 6-12 months?
	* What skills or knowledge do I need to acquire to reach my goals?

**Goal-Setting Strategies:**

1. **SMART goals**: Make your goals Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound.
2. **Break it down**: Divide large goals into smaller, manageable tasks to maintain momentum and motivation.
3. **Create an accountability system**: Share your goals with your partner or a trusted friend and ask them to hold you accountable.
4. **Celebrate progress**: Acknowledge and celebrate your progress along the way to stay motivated and encouraged.

2023/01/27 (Fri) 12:42 user: I've been keeping track of my bike mileage, and as of last week, I've clocked 347 miles since the start of the year. My goal is to reach 1000 miles by the end of summer. Do you have any tips on how to stay motivated to keep riding and reach my goal?
2023/01/27 (Fri) 12:42 assistant: Congratulations on tracking your mileage and setting a goal! Reaching 1000 miles by the end of summer is an achievable goal, and with a solid plan, you can stay motivated and crush it!

Here are some tips to help you stay motivated and reach your goal:

1. **Break your goal into smaller milestones**: Divide your goal into smaller, manageable chunks. For example, aim to ride 200 miles per month or 50 miles per week. This will make your goal feel less daunting and give you a sense of accomplishment as you reach each milestone.
2. **Create a routine**: Establish a regular riding schedule, whether it's daily, every other day, or a few times a week. Consistency is key to developing a habit and making progress towards your goal.
3. **Vary your route**: Mix up your route to avoid boredom and keep things interesting. Explore new neighborhoods, trails, or bike paths to discover new sights and challenges.
4. **Find a riding buddy**: Having someone to ride with can be a great motivator. You can encourage and support each other, share tips, and make the experience more enjoyable.
5. **Track your progress**: Continue tracking your mileage, and consider using a cycling app or spreadsheet to monitor your progress. Seeing your numbers grow can be a great motivator.
6. **Reward yourself**: Set small rewards for reaching certain milestones, like a new bike accessory, a post-ride coffee, or a celebratory dinner. This will give you something to look forward to and make the journey more enjoyable.
7. **Focus on the benefits**: Remember why you started riding in the first place. Focus on the benefits of cycling, such as improved health, reduced stress, and increased energy. This will help you stay motivated and committed to your goal.
8. **Be flexible**: Life can be unpredictable, and some days you might not feel like riding. Don't be too hard on yourself if you miss a day or two. Instead, adjust your schedule and get back on track as soon as possible.
9. **Celebrate your progress**: Acknowledge and celebrate your progress along the way. You've already clocked 347 miles, which is a great achievement! Recognize your hard work and use it as motivation to keep pushing forward.
10. **Make it fun**: Most importantly, remember to enjoy the ride! Listen to music, take in the scenery, and appreciate the freedom and joy that comes with cycling.

By following these tips, you'll be well on your way to reaching your goal of 1000 miles by the end of summer. Stay motivated, stay committed, and most importantly, have fun!
